candidates.title: Completion-token volume varies ~6x between model families on identical work — budget output tokens from measurement, not window count
candidates.body:
Two providers ran the same reconstruction (same lecture, same method llm-reconstruct/1.1.0, same window plan, 19 successful windows each) and their completion-token bills differ by ~5.7x: openai/gpt-oss-120b emitted 18,844 completion tokens where gemini-3.5-flash emitted 3,281, against similar prompt-side totals (27,891 vs 22,420). A reasoning-style model spends output tokens on deliberation even when the requested artifact (a small JSON object per window) is identical.

Consequence: a cost or rate-limit budget derived from window count plus expected artifact size will be wrong by the model family's verbosity factor — and on providers that charge rate-limit budget on the reservation (input + max_tokens), the verbosity also forces a larger max_tokens reservation, compounding the effect. Measure one real run per model family and budget from the ledger, not the plan.
candidates.basis: processing_runs rows 92069828 (gemini/gemini-3.5-flash: 19 successful calls, 22,420 prompt / 3,281 completion) and ff0721de (groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b: 19 successful calls, 27,891 prompt / 18,844 completion), same lecture and method/version, read in this session's read-only ledger query. Confidence medium: one lecture, one pair of models — the ~6x figure is real but its generality is a single comparison.
evidence_refs: processing_runs rows 92069828-ebab-4cdd-94f1-c0f0cc9a84da and ff0721de-5b4b-479f-9bfa-3b3b6fea8dd0 (live database; query documented in this entry's session.md)
